measured_vs_declared._purpose: R-F1.1: the declared injection list MUST NEVER be used as ground truth. Recorded here exactly as measured, not adjusted to hit any target.
measured_vs_declared.superseded_note: Two supersessions on record, kept in order (drift is the useful part of the record, not overwritten): (1) version-2->3 (task 4.3, this revision): the Expected:/Received: cut regex only matched an UNPREFIXED line ('Expected: 5'); Jest's structural .toMatchObject()/.toEqual() diff format instead prefixes that summary line with a unified-diff marker ('- Expected  - 2' / '+ Received  + 2'), which the un-widened regex never matched, so the ENTIRE diff body (every differing property value) stayed in signature_text. Found on v2's amplified parseTransfers cause (146 failing generated cases collapsing into 146 DISTINCT clusters, one per case - the exact 'cluster count grows with case_count' normalizer defect tasks.md:602 names). Fixed by allowing an optional diff-marker character before the whitespace. Only c4 (the .toMatchObject failure) changed value here: signature da54112bb72162e0 -> 7f2043443e4b144b, signature_text shrank from the full multi-line diff dump to the bare matcher head 'Error: expect(received).toMatchObject(expected)'. c1-c3 (all '.toBe()' scalar heads, already unprefixed) are byte-identical to their version-2 values. Cluster count, cluster_id assignment (c1-c4, unchanged - the new c4 signature still sorts last ascending), R0's cluster_ids, and identifier_set_digest are ALL unchanged; only one signature VALUE changed. (2) version-1->2 (PR4-signature-scope-fix, kept verbatim below rather than overwritten): This replaced the normalizer_version 1 measurement of this identical committed src/ (same 3 injections, same 4 failing test_ids, same identifier_set_digest). Under version 1, the signature was hash(normalized_head) only, and all 3 causes' first-reported failures shared the same generic Jest '.toBe()' equality head text with nothing before the Expected:/Received: cut, so they collapsed into ONE cluster (signature 277580d674667852, count 3) alongside a second, already-distinct cluster (parseTransfers' toMatchObject failure, signature 2df32737777805ca) - 2 clusters total for 3 causes. Under version 2, the signature is hash(normalized_head + test_file); the three previously-merged failures are now in three different files (applyKeypadInput.test.ts, confirmSeed.test.ts, parseTransfers.test.ts) and so get three different signatures - 4 clusters total for 4 failures, one cluster per failure in this fixture, not per cause.
measured_vs_declared.finding: All 3 declared causes remain independently observable (none produced zero failures in isolation, so none was rejected under R-F1.2) - isolation measured 1, 1 and 2 failing cases respectively (applyKeypadInput, confirmSeed, parseTransfers), summing to 4, exactly the combined-run total (re-verified: each isolated injection's signature is byte-identical to its signature inside the combined run). The over-collapse defect measured under normalizer_version 1 (three unrelated causes in three different modules sharing one cluster because Jest's generic '.toBe()' head carried no distinguishing text) is closed: each of the 4 measured failures now has its own distinct cluster (c1-c4), and the bounded clusters view (design.md 9b) now also carries each cluster's distinct_test_files, so a diagnostician reading only that view can see cluster c1/c2/c3 each span exactly one module and c4 is parseTransfers' second, already-known-and-absorbed head. The remaining 2-clusters-for-1-cause split on parseTransfers.ts:34 (c1 '.toBe' head, c4 '.toMatchObject' head) is OVER-SPLIT, not over-collapse, and is the case design.md already names and absorbs by design: 'where a cause genuinely produces several heads..., slice 3b measures that count and R0 records the many-to-one mapping. The key absorbs it; the algorithm does not change' (design.md:449-450) - R0 above records cluster_ids [c1, c4] for that one cause_site accordingly, unchanged in shape from the version-1 measurement's own R0 for the same cause. Scope limit, stated rather than assumed: this fixture's three modules are import-free by construction (PR3a-i's own independence check), so no single cause here could legitimately span two test files; a signature scoped by test file is therefore safe against introducing a NEW over-split failure mode in THIS fixture. A future fixture whose modules import each other could let one real cause produce failures in two files, which this rule would then over-split - R0's many-to-one mapping is what absorbs that case too, not a reason to loosen the signature.
